q-48845.name: Question 1
q-48845.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(2)=1,\,{f}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{2},\,g(2)=6,\,{g}^{′}(2)=3
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=2.$
q-48845.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=2} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(2)g(2)-f(2){g}^{′}(2)}{{g}^{2}(2)} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6-1\cdot 3}{{6}^{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

For the functions f(x) and g(x), you are given the following data:

f(2)=1,f′(2)=12,g(2)=6,g′(2)=3

Compute ddx(f(x)g(x)) at x=2.

a
0

−14
c
14
d
16
e
−16
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the quotient rule, we get ddx(f(x)g(x))=f′(x)g(x)−f(x)g′(x)(g(x))2.

At the point where x=2, this gives

ddx(f(x)g(x))|x=2=f′(2)g(2)−f(2)g′(2)g2(2)=12⋅6−1⋅362=0.

q-48920.name: Question 2
q-48920.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=2$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $4$ | $3$ | $5$ | $1$ |

If $h(x)=(f(x)+1)(2g(x)-2),$ compute ${h}^{′}(2).$
q-48920.worked_solution:
The product rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(uv)=u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=f(x)+1$ and $v=2g(x)-2.$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={f}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2{g}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(f(x)+1)\cdot 2{g}^{′}(x)+(2g(x)-2)\cdot {f}^{′}(x) \\  & =2{g}^{′}(x)(f(x)+1)+2{f}^{′}(x)(g(x)-1).\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =2{g}^{′}(2)(f(2)+1)+2{f}^{′}(2)(g(2)-1) \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot (4+1)+2\cdot 5\cdot (3-1) \\  & =2\cdot 5+10\cdot 2 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

q-48920.html:
Question 2
?

The values of functions f(x) and g(x) and their derivatives at x=2 are given in the table below.

x f(x) g(x) f′(x) g′(x)
2 4 3 5 1

If h(x)=(f(x)+1)(2g(x)−2), compute h′(2).

a
17
b
32
c
25
d
30
e
24
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The product rule states that ddx(uv)=udvdx+vdudx.

Let u=f(x)+1 and v=2g(x)−2. Differentiating each, we get dudx=f′(x)anddvdx=2g′(x).

Substituting this into the product rule gives

h′(x)=udvdx+vdudx=(f(x)+1)⋅2g′(x)+(2g(x)−2)⋅f′(x)=2g′(x)(f(x)+1)+2f′(x)(g(x)−1).

At x=2, this gives

h′(2)=2g′(2)(f(2)+1)+2f′(2)(g(2)−1)=2⋅1⋅(4+1)+2⋅5⋅(3−1)=2⋅5+10⋅2=30.

q-72990.name: Question 3
q-72990.problem:
For the functions $v(x)$ and $w(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
v(2)=-3,\,{v}^{′}(2)=1,\,w(2)=-2,\,{w}^{′}(2)=-4
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(v(x)-2w(x))$ at $x=2.$
q-72990.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(v(x)-2w(x))={v}^{′}(x)-2{w}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(v(x)-2w(x))|}_{x=2} & ={v}^{′}(2)-2{w}^{′}(2) \\  & =1-2\cdot (-4) \\  & =1+8 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
